comments.body: rebar-debug evidence update: Runtime proof established two root-propagation defects. RunnerAgentStep and direct review_ticket loaded repository prompt metadata with a root but re-rendered the body without that same root, producing an empty project-only prompt. The code-review gate also computed an attested cfg.repo_path but passed the original live/None request root into project-criterion membership and batch validation, so an attested prompt could be skipped or rejected before the LLM. A sibling in scan_epics_for_spec had the same metadata/body split. RED/GREEN/mutation coverage now exercises all paths, including live-vs-snapshot metadata, body, criterion membership, and local fallback. The unchanged 8ac3d3c replay now completes the full gate, but the project finder abstains 5/5 in isolation because that changed clause does not satisfy the tightened three-part grounding instruction; its surviving advisory is therefore built-in, not lost project identity. A strict project FIRE fixture run through the same full four-pass workflow produced a surviving advisory with reviewer_id code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries, criteria project.review-phase-boundaries, block_threshold 0.9, and blocking_enabled false. This proves attribution survives through Pass 3 when the project finder emits. No voting or review-process semantics were changed.

## Context

The live negative dogfood probe on Gerrit change 986 patchset 2, revision 8ac3d3c1218c6a108fd6772f5b3686a883ad2415, added exactly `For each candidate finding, assign severity as high, medium, or low.` The review bot returned LLM-Review +1 with one advisory and persisted artifact cd39-137e-0afd-490e. The code_review_result_v2 payload proves llm_ran=true and correctly describes the cross-phase defect, but no surviving or dropped finding carries `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` or `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]`. The surfaced advisory instead carries built-in criteria `[correctness, regression, maintainability]`, threshold 0.95, and no reviewer identity. Its dependency snapshot includes the project prompt hash, so repository asset capture occurred, but the required project attribution is absent before artifact serialization. This blocks dogfood story 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d.

## Plan

- Reproduce the live identity loss locally through the real Round-A fan-in, finding merge/clustering, Pass-2 verification, and deterministic Pass-3 decision path using the exact negative directive.
- Trace where the project physical reviewer id and logical criterion id are lost or replaced, distinguishing non-execution from clustering/normalization loss.
- Add a RED regression at the smallest pipeline boundary that reproduces the live result shape, then preserve project attribution through Pass 3 and the v2 sidecar without altering built-in attribution.
- Re-run the same live negative revision after deployment; do not substitute a different probe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The precise changeable cause of the live missing project `reviewer_id` and logical `criteria` is proven with runtime evidence from the real pipeline.
- [ ] Automated coverage reproduces the live identity-loss shape before the fix and passes after it.
- [ ] A project finding retains `reviewer_id: code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` and `criteria: [project.review-phase-boundaries]` through clustering, Pass 2, Pass 3, and `code_review_result_v2` emission.
- [ ] Pass 3 applies the repository-effective project posture (`block_threshold: 0.90`, `blocking_enabled: false`) to that finding, while overlay-absent and built-in finding attribution remain unchanged.
- [ ] The repair lands through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments.
- [ ] The unchanged live negative probe is rerun after deployment and its shared artifact contains the required project reviewer/logical-criterion identity.
